arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Kilberg argued the state law strikes at ERISA's core. He claimed it purports to revoke designations upon divorce.
Ms. Mcdowell argued the statute relates to employee benefit plans. She claimed it conflicts with specific ERISA provisions.
Mr. Goldstein argued the conflict notion is mistaken. He explained what the statute does and why.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests if federal law overrides a state rule. The rule cancels beneficiary designations after divorce. the sides that brought the case say this violates ERISA. the opposing sides say the state law stands.
